registryLegalName: Solicitor Application to Expunge Records After a First-Offence Drug Conditional Discharge, S.C. Code § 44-53-450(b)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: A person not previously convicted of any offence under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or under any state or federal marijuana, stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drug statute, who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession of a controlled substance under § 44-53-370(c) or (d) or § 44-53-375(A), may be placed on probation without entry of a judgment of guilt, with the court discharging the person and dismissing the proceedings on fulfilment of the terms. The discharge is not a conviction for purposes of any disqualification or disability, and it may occur only once with respect to any person.

On dismissal and discharge the person may apply to the court for an order expunging from all official records, other than the retained nonpublic record, all recordation relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and the dismissal and discharge. If the court determines after hearing that the person was dismissed and discharged, it shall enter the order, restoring the person in the contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest.

Requires payment before discharge of a fee of three hundred fifty dollars in general sessions court or one hundred fifty dollars in summary court, waivable, reducible or suspendable only for indigency.
Requires the summary court judge to attest where the matter was in summary court.
Exempts the route from SLED verification and its fee.

counselFlags: South Carolina expungements start with either the Solicitor's Office or the summary court and use the official SCCA 223-series forms. LegalEase must not produce a substitute for an official South Carolina Judicial Branch form.
South Carolina generally expunges one charge per order, with special fee-treatment rules for related charges arising from the same incident under the Uniform Expungement Act.

A pardon is a separate process through the Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services and is NOT expungement. Do not file a pardon as an expungement and do not tell a participant that a pardon clears the record.

Court level varies: the conditional discharge itself may be entered in general sessions or in summary court, and the fee and attestor differ accordingly. Determine the court level and disposition first; no court is named by LegalEase.
No verification or notarization statute is identified for the § 44-53-450(B) application. Verification is a feature of the official SCCA form, which is not drafted here; nothing is filled.

Fee at source: § 44-53-450(C) requires payment before discharge of three hundred fifty dollars in general sessions court or one hundred fifty dollars in summary court. It is waivable, reducible or suspendable only for indigency. This is a source-established fee and may be stated to a participant, unlike the routes where the source is silent.
One-time route: the discharge and dismissal may occur only once with respect to any person, and a person previously convicted of a qualifying drug offence is excluded.

A nonpublic record is retained by the Department of Narcotic and Dangerous Drugs under SLED solely to determine whether a later offence is a subsequent one. The expungement does not reach that retained record, and a participant must be told so.
Where the terms and conditions were violated and the court entered an adjudication of guilt, the route is unavailable.
Section 44-53-450(B) requires the court to determine after a hearing that the person was dismissed and discharged. LegalEase never asserts that a hearing occurred or predicts its outcome.
The SLED verification fee is not charged for this route under § 17-22-940(E).

registryExcerpt.legalName: Solicitor Application to Expunge Records After a First-Offence Drug Conditional Discharge, S.C. Code § 44-53-450(b)
registryExcerpt.publicName: Clear a first South Carolina drug possession case that ended in a conditional discharge
registryExcerpt.venue: Statewide statute. The conditional discharge itself may be entered in general sessions or summary court; the expungement application runs through the Solicitor's Office in the circuit where the offence was committed.
registryExcerpt.destinationName: Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond fulfilment of the terms and conditions, the court's discharge and dismissal, and payment of the § 44-53-450(C) fee. Unlike several other states' conditional-discharge routes, § 44-53-450(B) imposes no post-discharge waiting period.

exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offence under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or under any state or federal statute relating to marijuana, or stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drugs.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under § 44-53-450; it may occur only once.
Any person whose terms and conditions were violated and against whom the court entered an adjudication of guilt.
Offences other than possession of a controlled substance under § 44-53-370(c) or (d) or § 44-53-375(A).
The nonpublic record retained by the Department of Narcotic and Dangerous Drugs under SLED, which the expungement order expressly does not reach.
Any case where the § 44-53-450(C) fee remains unpaid, since payment precedes discharge and dismissal.
